settings.definition_quote: Our setting involves $N$ agents with the same reward function $h$ defined on a domain $\mathcal{X}\subset \mathbb{R}^d$. ... In each iteration $t\in[T]$, every agent $i\in[N]$ receives a set $\mathcal{X}_{t,i}$ of $K$ context vectors and selects one of them $x_{t,i}$ to be queried to observe a noisy output $y_{t,i}= h(x_{t,i}) + \epsilon$ where $\epsilon$ is an $R$-sub-Gaussian noise. We will analyze the total cumulative regret $R_T = \sum_i\sum_t r_{t,i}$ where $r_{t,i} = h(x_{t,i}^*) - h(x_{t,i})$

source.label: theorem:regret
source.quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1)$, $\lambda=1+2/T$, and $D=\mathcal{O}(T / (N \widetilde{d}))$. Suppose that the NN width $m$ grows polynomially: $m \geq \text{poly}( \lambda, T, K, N, L, \log(1/\delta), 1/\lambda_0)$. For the gradient descent training, let $\eta=C_4(m\lambda + mTL)^{-1}$ ... and $J=\widetilde{O}(TL/(\lambda C_4))$. Then, with probability of at least $1-\delta$, $R_T = \widetilde{O}(\widetilde{d}\sqrt{TN} + \widetilde{d}_{\max} N \sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Analysed for simplified algorithm setting alpha=0 except first iteration of each epoch. Regret summed over N agents, against per-round best context.

source.label: theorem:communication
source.quote: With the same parameters as Theorem 1, if the NN width $m$ satisfies $m \geq \text{poly}(T, K, N, L, \log(1/\delta))$, then with probability of at least $1-\delta$, the total number of communication rounds for FN-UCB satisfies $C_T = \widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\widetilde{d}\sqrt{N})$.
